name: truSculpt iD
lead: truSculpt iD is a non-invasive radiofrequency (RF) body-contouring device from Cutera for localized fat reduction, with related truSculpt devices registered in trials since 2009.[4][5] Radiofrequency is one of several energy modalities used for non-invasive fat reduction, alongside cryotherapy, ultrasound and laser.[2]

Published evidence includes a 2020 ultrasound study of a temperature-controlled multi-frequency monopolar RF device on the abdomen and flanks,[2] a 2017 study of 1-MHz monopolar RF for lower facial fat,[1] and a series of registered truSculpt trials of 4 to 70 participants.[4][5][6]

paras: The abstract of a 2020 study describes high-frequency monopolar RF as raising fat temperature enough to reduce its thickness without excessively heating the skin.[2] A 2024 review in Clinics in Plastic Surgery mentions truSculpt flex, an electrical muscle stimulation device, among non-invasive tools one surgeon uses with surgery.[3]

A 2020 study in the Journal of Drugs in Dermatology used ultrasound to evaluate a single treatment with a temperature-controlled monopolar RF device for localized abdominal and flank adiposity; the authors noted that two devices had previously been shown to reduce fat thickness on ultrasound after one treatment.[2] A 2017 study of static monopolar 1-MHz RF assessed facial fat reduction and tightening of the lower face.[1] Full results were not available for this article.

Registered trials sponsored for the truSculpt device include a pivotal circumferential reduction study of 70 people for abdominal fat starting in 2016,[5] a 44-person thigh circumference study from 2012,[6] and smaller studies on lipolysis, wrinkles, cellulite and tissue tightening between 2017 and 2018.[7][8][9] Most records list the studies as completed, but no outcome data were retrieved.
No safety data specific to truSculpt iD were retrieved for this article.

timeline.event: A truSculpt thigh circumference reduction study is registered (terminated).[4]
Pivotal circumferential reduction study for abdominal fat begins.[5]
Several truSculpt pilot, follow-up and wrinkle studies begin.[7][8]

card.summary: A Cutera radiofrequency fat-reduction device with many small registered trials but few published results.
card.note: Outcome data for the specific device were not retrieved.

quick.overview:
truSculpt iD is a non-invasive radiofrequency device marketed for reducing localized fat. It sits alongside freezing, laser and ultrasound approaches.

Several small registered trials exist, plus published studies of related monopolar RF devices.
quick.mechanism: Radiofrequency energy heats fat tissue while the skin is kept cooler, with the aim of reducing fat thickness.
quick.risks: No device-specific safety data were retrieved.
